Euler step = 0.02.</p><div class=\"world-controls\"><button class=\"control\" data-world=\"hide-memory\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Hide the dashed line</button><button class=\"control\" data-world=\"couple-memory\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Stop the parts affecting each other</button></div><div class=\"world-result\" id=\"world-result\" aria-live=\"polite\">The solid and dashed lines show two parts that affect each other. Hiding a line only changes the picture.</div><p class=\"world-note\">SCHEMATIC NUMERICAL ILLUSTRATION · NOT THE CORPUS REPLAY</p></div>",
      "instruction": "First hide a line. Then disconnect the link. Compare what each action changes.",
      "note": "A small computer calculation that explains an idea. It is not the larger research experiment.",
      "type": "memory"
    },
    "erasure": {
      "id": "erasure",
      "title": "What can one number tell you?",
      "html": "<div class=\"world-encounter\" data-world-type=\"erasure\" data-origin=\"a\" data-enriched=\"false\"><p class=\"encounter-label\">THE RECORD / TWO ORIGINS, ONE SUM</p><div class=\"erasure-record\"><span>ONLY NUMBER KEPT</span><strong>4</strong><small id=\"extra-record\" hidden>FIRST NUMBER: 1</small></div><div class=\"world-controls\"><button class=\"control\" data-world=\"origin\" data-value=\"a\" aria-pressed=\"true\">Consider (1, 3)</button><button class=\"control\" data-world=\"origin\" data-value=\"b\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Consider (2, 2)</button></div><button class=\"control enrich-control\" data-world=\"enrich\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Keep the first number too</button><div class=\"world-result\" id=\"world-result\" aria-live=\"polite\">Both pairs add up to 4. The sum alone cannot tell them apart.</div><p class=\"world-note\">A FINITE IDENTIFIABILITY EXAMPLE · AN ADDED RECORD IS NEW INFORMATION</p></div>",
      "instruction": "Try both pairs. Then keep a second record and see what becomes clear.",
      "note": "A small example of what a record keeps and leaves out.",
      "type": "erasure"
    },
    "attention": {
      "id": "attention",
      "title": "A close view and a broad view",
      "html": "<div class=\"world-encounter\" data-world-type=\"attention\" data-view=\"broad\"><p class=\"encounter-label\">THE CANOPY / CHANGE A PRESENTATION</p><div class=\"attention-canopy\" role=\"img\" aria-label=\"Five named details in a stylized clearing\"><span class=\"canopy-detail detail-leaf\" style=\"__CSS_attention_0__\"><i aria-hidden=\"true\"></i>Leaf</span><span class=\"canopy-detail detail-bird\" style=\"__CSS_attention_1__\"><i aria-hidden=\"true\"></i>Bird</span><span class=\"canopy-detail detail-path\" style=\"__CSS_attention_2__\"><i aria-hidden=\"true\"></i>Path</span><span class=\"canopy-detail detail-wind\" style=\"__CSS_attention_3__\"><i aria-hidden=\"true\"></i>Wind</span><span class=\"canopy-detail detail-water\" style=\"__CSS_attention_4__\"><i aria-hidden=\"true\"></i>Water</span><div class=\"canopy-lens\" aria-hidden=\"true\"></div></div><div class=\"world-controls\"><button class=\"control\" data-world=\"attention\" data-value=\"broad\" aria-pressed=\"true\">View the whole clearing</button><button class=\"control\" data-world=\"attention\" data-value=\"focus\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Look closely at the leaf</button></div><div class=\"world-result\" id=\"world-result\" aria-live=\"polite\">The broad view keeps several relationships available.</div><p class=\"world-note\">AN ILLUSTRATION OF A VIEW · NOT A TEST OF YOUR ATTENTION</p></div>",
      "instruction": "Try the broad view and the close view. Notice what each brings forward.",
      "note": "A change to the drawing, not an assessment of your attention.",
      "type": "attention"
    },
    "will": {
      "id": "will",
      "title": "From choosing to acting",
      "html": "<div class=\"world-encounter\" data-world-type=\"will\"><p class=\"encounter-label\">THE JOINS / A CONCEPTUAL SEQUENCE</p><div class=\"relation-emblem emblem-will\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><i></i><i></i><i></i></div><p class=\"world-intro\">An arrow is a question about a relationship.</p><div class=\"deck-options\"><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"0\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Getting ready → choosing<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"1\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Choosing → acting<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"2\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Acting → learning what happened<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button></div><div class=\"world-result\" id=\"deck-result\" aria-live=\"polite\">Open a question. You may inspect every view.</div></div>",
      "instruction": "Open each link to see what would be needed to explain it.",
      "note": "",
      "type": "will"
    },
    "stone": {
      "id": "stone",
      "title": "Three ways to investigate a stone",
      "html": "<div class=\"world-encounter\" data-world-type=\"stone\"><p class=\"encounter-label\">THE STONE / THREE INVESTIGATIVE LENSES</p><svg class=\"stone-drawing\" viewBox=\"0 0 360 280\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><defs><linearGradient id=\"stoneFace\"><stop stop-color=\"#b7a48a\"/><stop offset=\"1\" stop-color=\"#534c4a\"/></linearGradient></defs><path d=\"m65 110 120-62 126 72-20 94-139 28-90-63Z\" fill=\"url(#stoneFace)\"/><path d=\"m65 110 124 61 122-51M189 171l-37 71M185 48l4 123\"/><path class=\"stone-marks\" d=\"m95 128 52 26m-54-14 52 26m-52-14 48 24m64 22 62-13m-64 24 61-13\"/><g class=\"stone-context\"><circle cx=\"185\" cy=\"145\" r=\"118\"/><path d=\"M25 235h310M185 10v28m0 220v17\"/></g></svg><p class=\"world-intro\">An illustrative object. No sampled monument is represented.</p><div class=\"deck-options\"><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"0\" aria-pressed=\"false\">What it is made of<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"1\" aria-pressed=\"false\">How it was shaped<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"2\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Where it was found<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button></div><div class=\"world-result\" id=\"deck-result\" aria-live=\"polite\">Open a question. You may inspect every view.</div></div>",
      "instruction": "Choose a view of the stone. Each asks for a different kind of evidence.",
      "note": "",
      "type": "stone"
    },
    "preservation": {
      "id": "preservation",
      "title": "Why might a mark be missing?",
      "html": "<div class=\"world-encounter\" data-world-type=\"preservation\"><p class=\"encounter-label\">THE SURVIVING RECORD / LAYERS OF INFERENCE</p><svg class=\"stone-drawing\" viewBox=\"0 0 360 280\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><defs><linearGradient id=\"stoneFace\"><stop stop-color=\"#b7a48a\"/><stop offset=\"1\" stop-color=\"#534c4a\"/></linearGradient></defs><path d=\"m65 110 120-62 126 72-20 94-139 28-90-63Z\" fill=\"url(#stoneFace)\"/><path d=\"m65 110 124 61 122-51M189 171l-37 71M185 48l4 123\"/><path class=\"stone-marks\" d=\"m95 128 52 26m-54-14 52 26m-52-14 48 24m64 22 62-13m-64 24 61-13\"/><g class=\"stone-context\"><circle cx=\"185\" cy=\"145\" r=\"118\"/><path d=\"M25 235h310M185 10v28m0 220v17\"/></g></svg><p class=\"world-intro\">Which explanation could account for an absent trace?</p><div class=\"deck-options\"><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"0\" aria-pressed=\"false\">The process never occurred<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"1\" aria-pressed=\"false\">The trace was altered<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"2\" aria-pressed=\"false\">The detector missed it<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button></div><div class=\"world-result\" id=\"deck-result\" aria-live=\"polite\">Open a question. You may inspect every view.</div></div>",
      "instruction": "Choose a reason a trace might be missing. Read what would need checking.",
      "note": "",
      "type": "preservation"
    },
    "tiling": {
      "id": "tiling",
      "title": "Apply a counting rule",
      "html": "<div class=\"world-encounter\" data-world-type=\"tiling\" data-step=\"0\"><p class=\"encounter-label\">THE PATTERNED WALL / AN EXACT COUNT ACTION</p><svg class=\"rosette\" viewBox=\"0 0 300 300\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><g><path d=\"m150 30 28 80-28 46-28-46Z\" transform=\"rotate(0 150 150)\"/><path d=\"m150 30 28 80-28 46-28-46Z\" transform=\"rotate(36 150 150)\"/><path d=\"m150 30 28 80-28 46-28-46Z\" transform=\"rotate(72 150 150)\"/><path d=\"m150 30 28 80-28 46-28-46Z\" transform=\"rotate(108 150 150)\"/><path d=\"m150 30 28 80-28 46-28-46Z\" transform=\"rotate(144 150 150)\"/><path d=\"m150 30 28 80-28 46-28-46Z\" transform=\"rotate(180 150 150)\"/><path d=\"m150 30 28 80-28 46-28-46Z\" transform=\"rotate(216 150 150)\"/><path d=\"m150 30 28 80-28 46-28-46Z\" transform=\"rotate(252 150 150)\"/><path d=\"m150 30 28 80-28 46-28-46Z\" transform=\"rotate(288 150 150)\"/><path d=\"m150 30 28 80-28 46-28-46Z\" transform=\"rotate(324 150 150)\"/></g><circle cx=\"150\" cy=\"150\" r=\"120\"/><circle cx=\"150\" cy=\"150\" r=\"68\"/></svg><div class=\"count-pair\"><span><small>FIRST NUMBER</small><strong id=\"count-a\">1</strong></span><span><small>SECOND NUMBER</small><strong id=\"count-b\">1</strong></span></div><p class=\"equation-note\">(a, b) → (2a + b, a + b)</p><div class=\"world-controls\"><button class=\"control\" data-world=\"inflate\">Apply the rule once</button><button class=\"control\" data-world=\"reset-pattern\">Reset the pair</button></div><div class=\"world-result\" id=\"world-result\" aria-live=\"polite\">Step 0. Begin with the declared pair (1, 1).</div><p class=\"world-note\">EXACT INTEGER COUNTS · THE ROSETTE IS DECORATIVE</p></div>",
      "instruction": "Apply the rule one step at a time. Watch the two numbers. Reset to begin again.",
      "note": "The number rule is exact. The ornament is decorative.",
      "type": "tiling"
    },
    "code": {
      "id": "code",
      "title": "Try a simple error-correcting message",
      "html": "<div class=\"world-encounter\" data-world-type=\"code\" data-original=\"0\"><p class=\"encounter-label\">THE REPAIR BENCH / A THREE-BIT REPETITION CODE</p><div class=\"world-controls\"><button class=\"control\" data-world=\"original-bit\" data-value=\"0\" aria-pressed=\"true\">Start with zero</button><button class=\"control\" data-world=\"original-bit\" data-value=\"1\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Start with one</button></div><p class=\"world-intro\">Flip any of the three received bits.</p><div class=\"bit-word\"><button data-world=\"flip-bit\" data-value=\"0\" aria-pressed=\"false\" aria-label=\"Received bit 1: zero\">0</button><button data-world=\"flip-bit\" data-value=\"1\" aria-pressed=\"false\" aria-label=\"Received bit 2: zero\">0</button><button data-world=\"flip-bit\" data-value=\"2\" aria-pressed=\"false\" aria-label=\"Received bit 3: zero\">0</button></div><div class=\"world-result\" id=\"world-result\" aria-live=\"polite\">Decoder returns 0. The received word matches the original bit.</div><p class=\"world-note\">A DECLARED TOY CODE · ONE FLIP IS CORRECTABLE, TWO ARE NOT GUARANTEED</p></div>",
      "instruction": "Choose a starting bit: zero or one. Flip one of the three bits, then a second. Watch the decoded answer.",
      "note": "A small example code. One flipped bit can be repaired; two can give the wrong answer.",
      "type": "code"
    },
    "laboratory": {
      "id": "laboratory",
      "title": "Choose a way to compare explanations",
      "html": "<div class=\"world-encounter\" data-world-type=\"laboratory\"><p class=\"encounter-label\">THE BENCH / CHOOSE A DISCRIMINATOR</p><div class=\"relation-emblem emblem-laboratory\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><i></i><i></i><i></i></div><p class=\"world-intro\">A proposal for a record, not a stream of acquired data.</p><div class=\"deck-options\"><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"0\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Add a timing reference<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"1\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Reverse the path<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"2\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Change the waiting time<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button></div><div class=\"world-result\" id=\"deck-result\" aria-live=\"polite\">Open a question. You may inspect every view.</div></div>",
      "instruction": "Choose a comparison to see which difference it could reveal.",
      "note": "",
      "type": "laboratory"
    },
    "cost": {
      "id": "cost",
      "title": "Compare what returns with what is lost",
      "html": "<div class=\"world-encounter\" data-world-type=\"cost\"><p class=\"encounter-label\">THE RATE CARDS / REPORTED SOFTWARE RESULTS</p><div class=\"rate-controls\"><button data-world=\"rate\" data-value=\"0\" aria-pressed=\"false\"><small>SETTING</small><strong>4</strong></button><button data-world=\"rate\" data-value=\"1\" aria-pressed=\"true\"><small>SETTING</small><strong>8</strong></button><button data-world=\"rate\" data-value=\"2\" aria-pressed=\"false\"><small>SETTING</small><strong>16</strong></button><button data-world=\"rate\" data-value=\"3\" aria-pressed=\"false\"><small>SETTING</small><strong>32</strong></button></div><div class=\"ledger-bars\"><label>How much returns in the wanted form <output id=\"rate-overlap\">98.77%</output></label><div><i id=\"overlap-bar\" style=\"__CSS_cost_0__\"></i></div><label>How much is lost <output id=\"rate-loss\">1.59%</output></label><div><i id=\"loss-bar\" style=\"__CSS_cost_1__\"></i></div></div><div class=\"world-result\" id=\"world-result\" aria-live=\"polite\">Setting 8 gives the largest return in the wanted form among these four tested settings.</div><p class=\"world-note\">REPORTED METERED-MODEL VALUES · NOT A HARDWARE MEASUREMENT</p></div>",
      "instruction": "Choose a setting. A larger number means a slower loop here. Compare how much signal returns with how much is lost.",
      "note": "Reported computer results. Percentages are rounded to two decimal places.",
      "type": "cost"
    },
    "cosmos": {
      "id": "cosmos",
      "title": "Three open questions in physics",
      "html": "<div class=\"world-encounter\" data-world-type=\"cosmos\"><p class=\"encounter-label\">THE OBSERVATORY / OPEN WINDOWS</p><div class=\"question-sky\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_0__\"></i><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_1__\"></i><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_2__\"></i><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_3__\"></i><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_4__\"></i><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_5__\"></i><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_6__\"></i><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_7__\"></i><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_8__\"></i><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_9__\"></i><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_10__\"></i><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_11__\"></i><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_12__\"></i><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_13__\"></i><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_14__\"></i><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_15__\"></i><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_16__\"></i><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_17__\"></i><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_18__\"></i><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_19__\"></i><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_20__\"></i><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_21__\"></i><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_22__\"></i><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_23__\"></i><i style=\"__CSS_cosmos_24__\"></i><span>?</span></div><p class=\"world-intro\">The stars are an illustration. The gates are research questions.</p><div class=\"deck-options\"><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"0\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Gravity & torsion<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"1\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Flavour & neutrinos<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"2\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Cosmic history<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button></div><div class=\"world-result\" id=\"deck-result\" aria-live=\"polite\">Open a question. You may inspect every view.</div></div>",

    "scale": {
      "id": "scale",
      "title": "What changes when you group the cells?",
      "html": "<div class=\"world-encounter\" data-world-type=\"scale\"><p class=\"encounter-label\">THE CHANGING SCALE / A FIXED FOUR-BY-FOUR PATTERN</p><div class=\"scale-grid\" id=\"scale-grid\" role=\"img\" aria-label=\"Fine checkerboard with eight filled cells\"><span style=\"__CSS_scale_0__\">1</span><span style=\"__CSS_scale_1__\">0</span><span style=\"__CSS_scale_2__\">1</span><span style=\"__CSS_scale_3__\">0</span><span style=\"__CSS_scale_4__\">0</span><span style=\"__CSS_scale_5__\">1</span><span style=\"__CSS_scale_6__\">0</span><span style=\"__CSS_scale_7__\">1</span><span style=\"__CSS_scale_8__\">1</span><span style=\"__CSS_scale_9__\">0</span><span style=\"__CSS_scale_10__\">1</span><span style=\"__CSS_scale_11__\">0</span><span style=\"__CSS_scale_12__\">0</span><span style=\"__CSS_scale_13__\">1</span><span style=\"__CSS_scale_14__\">0</span><span style=\"__CSS_scale_15__\">1</span></div><div class=\"world-controls\"><button class=\"control\" data-world=\"scale\" data-value=\"1\" aria-pressed=\"true\">Individual cells</button><button class=\"control\" data-world=\"scale\" data-value=\"2\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Groups of four</button><button class=\"control\" data-world=\"scale\" data-value=\"4\" aria-pressed=\"false\">One group</button></div><div class=\"world-result\" id=\"world-result\" aria-live=\"polite\">The total is 8. The fine view also preserves where the eight filled cells are.</div><p class=\"world-note\">A DECLARED BLOCK-AVERAGING EXAMPLE · NOT A RENORMALIZATION THEOREM</p></div>",
      "instruction": "Combine the cells into bigger blocks. Look for what stays the same and what disappears.",
      "note": "An example of grouping information, not a proof about physics.",
      "type": "scale"
    },
    "coexistence": {
      "id": "coexistence",
      "title": "Read a computer model’s results",
      "html": "<div class=\"world-encounter\" data-world-type=\"scenario\"><p class=\"encounter-label\">THE SHARED-WORLD RECORD / INSPECT A CONDITION</p><div class=\"relation-emblem emblem-scenario\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><i></i><i></i><i></i></div><p class=\"world-intro\">Reported synthetic results. This is not a live policy simulator.</p><div class=\"deck-options\"><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"0\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Lower urgency<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"1\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Higher urgency<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"2\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Keep the tradeoffs<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button></div><div class=\"world-result\" id=\"deck-result\" aria-live=\"polite\">Open a question. You may inspect every view.</div></div>",
      "instruction": "Open each part of the computer result. Keep its limits beside its ranking.",
      "note": "",
      "type": "scenario"
    },
    "weights": {
      "id": "weights",
      "title": "What should the score value?",
      "html": "<div class=\"world-encounter\" data-world-type=\"weights\"><p class=\"encounter-label\">THE WEIGHT DESK / DECLARED TOY QUANTITIES</p><p class=\"world-intro\">Scores: speed / thoroughness. Each plan is good at a different thing.</p><div class=\"weight-options\"><div><span>OPTION A</span><strong>8 / 2</strong></div><div><span>OPTION B</span><strong>2 / 8</strong></div></div><p class=\"equation-note\">Score = w × speed + (1 − w) × thoroughness</p><label class=\"range-label\" for=\"weight-input\">How much should speed count? <output id=\"weight-label\">50%</output></label><input class=\"world-range\" id=\"weight-input\" data-world-input=\"weights\" type=\"range\" min=\"0\" max=\"100\" value=\"50\"><div class=\"weight-scores\"><span>A <output id=\"score-a\">5.00</output></span><span>B <output id=\"score-b\">5.00</output></span></div><div class=\"world-result\" id=\"world-result\" aria-live=\"polite\">The two plans have the same score with these priorities.</div><p class=\"world-note\">INVENTED NUMBERS · NO PEOPLE OR OUTCOMES ARE SCORED</p></div>",
      "instruction": "Move the slider to change what the score values. The options themselves stay the same.",
      "note": "Invented scores for two imaginary plans. No people are scored.",
      "type": "weights"
    },
    "hiddenness": {
      "id": "hiddenness",
      "title": "An optional religious reading",
      "html": "<div class=\"world-encounter\" data-world-type=\"horizon\"><p class=\"encounter-label\">THE QUIET HORIZON / AN OPTIONAL THEOLOGICAL READING</p><div class=\"meaning-landscape\"><div class=\"meaning-sun\" aria-hidden=\"true\"></div><div class=\"meaning-ridge\" aria-hidden=\"true\"></div><p>A question can remain open.</p></div><p class=\"world-intro\">The source begins by assuming God exists. This is an identified interpretation, not a premise of the experiments.</p><p class=\"world-note\">NO PERSONAL VERDICT · NO COMPULSORY CONCLUSION</p></div>",
      "instruction": "",
      "note": "You can leave the question open.",
      "type": "horizon"
    },
    "hope": {
      "id": "hope",
      "title": "An optional Christian account of hope",
      "html": "<div class=\"world-encounter\" data-world-type=\"horizon\"><p class=\"encounter-label\">THE QUIET HORIZON / AN OPTIONAL THEOLOGICAL READING</p><div class=\"meaning-landscape\"><div class=\"meaning-sun\" aria-hidden=\"true\"></div><div class=\"meaning-ridge\" aria-hidden=\"true\"></div><p>History is not denied.</p></div><p class=\"world-intro\">An explicitly Christian continuation. You may return to another path at any time.</p><p class=\"world-note\">NO PERSONAL VERDICT · NO COMPULSORY CONCLUSION</p></div>",
      "instruction": "",
      "note": "You can leave the question open.",
      "type": "horizon"

    "texts": {
      "id": "texts",
      "title": "Different kinds of evidence for a reading",
      "html": "<div class=\"world-encounter\" data-world-type=\"texts\"><p class=\"encounter-label\">THE READING DESK / KEEP THE RUNGS DISTINCT</p><div class=\"relation-emblem emblem-texts\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><i></i><i></i><i></i></div><p class=\"world-intro\">No forecasts or dates are generated here.</p><div class=\"deck-options\"><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"0\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Literary fit<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"1\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Historical correspondence<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"2\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Try it on fresh examples<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button></div><div class=\"world-result\" id=\"deck-result\" aria-live=\"polite\">Open a question. You may inspect every view.</div></div>",
      "instruction": "Open each kind of evidence. Notice why one does not automatically establish the next.",

      "type": "texts"

You may inspect every view.</div></div>",

    "closedpath": {
      "id": "closedpath",
      "title": "Different kinds of failure",
      "html": "<div class=\"world-encounter\" data-world-type=\"refusal\"><p class=\"encounter-label\">THE REFUSAL CABINET / WHAT KIND OF LIMIT?</p><div class=\"relation-emblem emblem-refusal\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><i></i><i></i><i></i></div><p class=\"world-intro\">Illustrative classifications from the negative-result discipline.</p><div class=\"deck-options\"><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"0\" aria-pressed=\"false\">A broken implementation<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"1\" aria-pressed=\"false\">A limit under certain conditions<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"2\" aria-pressed=\"false\">A proof of a limit<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button><button data-world=\"deck\" data-value=\"3\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Insufficient information<span aria-hidden=\"true\">↳</span></button></div><div class=\"world-result\" id=\"deck-result\" aria-live=\"polite\">Open a question. You may inspect every view.</div></div>",
      "instruction": "Choose a kind of failure. Read what it rules out and what it leaves open.",
      "note": "",
      "type": "refusal"
    }
  },
  "conversation": {
    "opening": "“I know the plan makes sense. I’m not sure I can keep doing it.”",
    "replies": [
      {
        "label": "Offer a more efficient plan",
        "answer": "“That might help later. I was trying to tell you what it is costing me.”",
        "question": "The problem you solved may be adjacent to the one being offered."
      },
      {
        "label": "Ask what has become difficult",
        "answer": "“It feels as though the plan has become more important than the people in it.”",
        "question": "A question can make room for information the plan did not contain."
      },
      {
        "label": "Ask what they need from this conversation",
        "answer": "“Could we work out what to keep, and what I’m allowed to put down?”",
        "question": "The speaker gets a chance to help define the encounter."
      }
    ]
  },

  "decks": {
    "will": {
      "heading": "THE JOINS / A CONCEPTUAL SEQUENCE",
      "intro": "An arrow is a question about a relationship.",
      "items": [
        [
          "Getting ready → choosing",
          "Which conditions make an option available, and what evidence shows it was selected?"
        ],
        [
          "Choosing → acting",
          "How does a choice lead to a bodily action? Wanting to move does not explain each step."
        ],
        [
          "Acting → learning what happened",
          "What record returns, and can it change the next action? A drawn loop is not proof that it ran."
        ]
      ]
    },
    "stone": {
      "heading": "THE STONE / THREE INVESTIGATIVE LENSES",
      "intro": "An illustrative object. No sampled monument is represented.",
      "items": [
        [
          "What it is made of",
          "Compare the minerals and texture with stone from known places. Knowing its name does not tell us where it came from."
        ],
        [
          "How it was shaped",
          "A proposed process should predict removal, tool wear, waste and surface traces together. A successful modern treatment is not evidence that it was used historically."
        ],
        [
          "Where it was found",
          "Where was it found? In which layer of the ground? What was nearby, and how old was it? These details help us understand its history."
        ]
      ]
    },
    "preservation": {
      "heading": "THE SURVIVING RECORD / LAYERS OF INFERENCE",
      "intro": "Which explanation could account for an absent trace?",
      "items": [
        [
          "The process never occurred",
          "Look for independent evidence about the candidate process and its predicted traces. Absence is informative only relative to expected detection."
        ],
        [
          "The trace was altered",
          "A preservation model would need exposure, burial, chemical change or conservation conditions tied to this object."
        ],
        [
          "The detector missed it",
          "Calibration, resolution and sampling determine what a null reading can exclude. More confidence in the same blind view does not fix it."
        ]
      ]
    },
    "laboratory": {
      "heading": "THE BENCH / CHOOSE A DISCRIMINATOR",
      "intro": "A proposal for a record, not a stream of acquired data.",
      "items": [
        [
          "Add a timing reference",
          "Compare the timing of signals that look alike when you measure only their height. Check the accuracy and stability of the timing reference too."
        ],
        [
          "Reverse the path",
          "Ask which part changes sign or order when a controlled path reverses. Ordinary noncommutativity remains a rival to test."
        ],
        [
          "Change the waiting time",
          "Record ring-downs, delays or dwell distributions. Equal endpoints can hide different histories and escape processes."
        ]
      ]
    },
    "cosmos": {
      "heading": "THE OBSERVATORY / OPEN WINDOWS",
      "intro": "The stars are an illustration. The gates are research questions.",
      "items": [
        [
          "Gravity & torsion",
          "The studied route has not justified the numbers needed for a physical gravity model. The source names particular changes that could reopen it. Naming a mathematical structure does not supply those numbers."
        ],
        [
          "Flavour & neutrinos",
          "The model still needs to calculate the relationships between particle types while respecting the theory’s rules. Inserting the desired relationships does not explain them."
        ],
        [
          "Cosmic history",
          "One model needs to explain expansion, small fluctuations, bending of light and large structures with the same settings. A separate fit for each observation does not yet do that."
        ]
      ]
    },
    "scenario": {
      "heading": "THE SHARED-WORLD RECORD / INSPECT A CONDITION",
      "intro": "Reported synthetic results. This is not a live policy simulator.",
      "items": [
        [
          "Lower urgency",
          "When the model assumes delivery succeeds, its overall score favours mediation in all 40 lower-urgency cases tested. That result depends on what the model measures and how it scores those things."
        ],
        [
          "Higher urgency",
          "Under the same assumptions, the overall score favours immediate visible action in all 120 higher-urgency cases tested. A result in this computer model does not give permission to act in a real community."
        ],
        [
          "Keep the tradeoffs",
          "Every case still involves a tradeoff: the option with the higher overall score is not better on every measure. The model still needs checks against real observations and evidence about causes."
        ]
      ]
    },
    "texts": {
      "heading": "THE READING DESK / KEEP THE RUNGS DISTINCT",
      "intro": "No forecasts or dates are generated here.",
      "items": [
        [
          "Literary fit",
          "A reading can fit a passage’s language and genre. The same narrative supplying oracle and outcome is a different kind of support from independent history."
        ],
        [
          "Historical correspondence",
          "Ask for the textual witness, source-date interval and independently dated outcome. Retrospective interpretation must remain available as a rival."
        ],
        [
          "Try it on fresh examples",
          "Choose the reading rule before trying it on examples you did not use to develop it. A good literary fit alone does not establish a divine source or show that a rule predicts better than its rivals."
        ]
      ]
    },
    "commons": {
      "heading": "THE COMMONS / WHAT A USEFUL PACKET CARRIES",
      "intro": "A proposal to another person. Nothing is sent by this reader.",
      "items": [
        [
          "The exact object",
          "State the question. Give the source file, version and original test or observation. Help someone else find exactly what you checked."
        ],
        [
          "The observed difference",
          "Separate what you expected from what happened, then state the narrow conclusion. Several summaries of one event do not become independent confirmations."
        ],
        [
          "The next opening",
          "Offer a reproduction command, a counterexample or the smallest useful next test. Inbox acceptance is not scientific admission or agreement."
        ]
      ]
    },
    "refusal": {
      "heading": "THE REFUSAL CABINET / WHAT KIND OF LIMIT?",
      "intro": "Illustrative classifications from the negative-result discipline.",
      "items": [
        [
          "A broken implementation",
          "The code did not perform the intended test. Repair and rerun can be appropriate; the failure does not settle the scientific claim."
        ],
        [
          "A limit under certain conditions",
          "A route fails under stated assumptions or in a parameter domain. A different declared assumption may reopen it."
        ],
        [
          "A proof of a limit",
          "The proof rules something out under its stated conditions. To reopen the question, explain which condition or part of the question has changed."
        ],
        [
          "Insufficient information",
          "The record cannot tell the competing explanations apart. Try a measurement that preserves the difference. Repeating the same limited measurement cannot recover what it leaves out."
        ]
      ]
    }
  },

Keep the interpretation open

The Field proposes retaining agency and correction. That is a contestable commitment, not a deduction from the calculations. Flexibility has costs; stable roles can be welcome; disagreement does not automatically imply dismissal. People affected by household decisions, including dependants, may have interests this two-person model does not represent.

Related questions

A household is also a relationship.

The Field holds this experiment because choices change what can happen next. These questions place the model beside the rest of the corpus:

  • Care

    what remains owed when an arrangement becomes difficult?

  • Revision

    what can be reopened, and who can ask?

  • Permission

    who authorizes a choice on someone else’s behalf?

  • Rupture and repair

    how might a relationship find contact again?

These relationships locate the example; they do not provide empirical validation for its authored rules.
